question: Article 3(5) of the Treaty of Lisbon sets out the objectives of the EU’s international relations as follows: ‘In its relations with the wider world, the Union shall uphold and promote its values and interests and contribute to the protection of its citizens.

It shall contribute to peace, security, the sustainable development of the Earth, solidarity and mutual respect among peoples, free and fair trade, eradication of poverty and the protection of human rights, in particular the rights of the child, as well as to the strict observance and the development of international law, including respect for the principles of the United Nations Charter.

’ On 3 January 2026, under President Donald Trump, the United States invaded Venezuela, bombing civilians and abducting Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro. Trump has since announced that the United States will now govern Venezuela. The United States’ actions are not promoting peace, security, solidarity or respect among peoples, and nor are they protecting human rights.
They are in flagrant violation of several international agreements, as well as being at odds with the principles underpinning the Charter of the United Nations. With the above in mind: 1.
For its part, how does the Commission intend to ensure that the objectives of the EU’s international relations as set out in the Treaty of Lisbon are met in its relations with the United States?
In their own communications, how and when are the Commissioners intending to condemn the United States’ violations of international law?

What action is the Commission intending to propose that the EU take against the United States in response to the illegal attack, in order to uphold the international relations principles enshrined in the Treaty of Lisbon?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (20.2.2026) International law and the principles of territorial integrity and state sovereignty enshrined in the UN Charter must be upheld under all circumstances. Members of the UN Security Council have a particular responsibility to uphold these principles.

This message was underscored in the 4 January 2026 statement by the High Representative/Vice-President supported by 26 Member States, as well as by President of the European Council and President of the Commission in their public reactions to the US intervention in Venezuela.

The EU has repeatedly stated that Nicolás Maduro lacks the legitimacy of a democratically elected president and has advocated for a Venezuelan-led peaceful transition to democracy in the country, respectful of its sovereignty. The right of the Venezuelan people to determine their future must be respected.

The Commission is in close contact with the US, as well as regional and international partners to support and facilitate dialogue with all parties involved, leading to a negotiated, democratic, inclusive and peaceful solution to the crisis, led by Venezuelans. The EU remains ready to continue engaging constructively with the US on all issues of common interest.

The EU continues to support an inclusive, rules-based multilateral system anchored in the principles of the UN Charter. The EU will continue to uphold the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and inviolability of borders together with other fundamental tenets of international law.
